body.v: Please find attached your October statement. Open the attachment and sign in to see the details.
If you have any questions, simply reply to this email.

hotspots.explain: The address looks right, but a sender address can be forged. Look instead at where your reply would go.
Replies would go to swissalpbank-mail.example, a different domain from the bank's. That mismatch is a classic trick.
"statement-october.pdf.html" ends in .html: it's a web page dressed up as a PDF. Once opened, it would show a fake sign-in page.
Anyone can pick up a first name online. It's no proof of identity.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Not the bank, despite the sender address. The reply-to address is on swissalpbank-mail.example: your reply would land with someone else.
choices: Your personal adviser at the bank

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: A little curiosity, nothing more: the message looks like an ordinary statement, on purpose. Nothing is rushing you.
choices: A little curiosity: it looks routine

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Open the attachment and sign in. That attachment is a web page that would collect your login details.
choices: Open the attachment and sign in

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Don't open it. Look for your statement in the SwissAlpBank app, or call the number on your card.
choices: Open the attachment to find out for sure
Reply and ask whether it's genuine

actions.label: Open the SwissAlpBank app yourself, under Documents
actions.consequence: Your statement is there, or not yet. Either way, the attachment stayed closed.

actions.label: Open the attachment to see the statement
actions.consequence: A fake sign-in page appears. If you enter your login details, the scammer gets them.

actions.label: Reply and ask whether the statement is genuine
actions.consequence: Your reply reaches the scammer, not the bank. They assure you everything is in order.

actions.label: Report it as phishing, then delete it

attacker_reveal: The sender was perfect, so you stopped looking. Meanwhile your replies were coming to me, and my "PDF" was a web page. Read a file name all the way to the last dot.
